intro: Iran is an Islamic republic where elected bodies sit under the authority of an unelected Supreme Leader.

chapters.title: How it works
text: The Supreme Leader, a senior cleric, controls the armed forces, courts and state media. Ali Khamenei held the post from 1989 until he was killed in 2026; his son Mojtaba Khamenei was then chosen. Voters elect a president and a parliament, the Majlis.
The Guardian Council vets candidates and laws, and many people are barred from standing.

chapters.title: Power and protest
text: The Revolutionary Guards are a powerful military force with big business interests. Human rights groups criticise Iran for arrests of protesters and use of the death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: A body that approves laws and election candidates.
